DESCRIPTION
  Set or clear one attribute on one requirement, or on every requirement matching a filter

USAGE
  symspec update [flags] <attr> [<value>]

ARGUMENTS
  attr string     The attribute to change. Legal values: patternType, preCondition, trigger, systemName, systemResponse, priority, status, verificationMethod, verificationNote, responseKind, stateEffect, stateConstraint.
NOT updatable, each for its own reason: `id` and `key` are immutable handles (every edge
references them), `sentence` is a denormalized rendering the next slot edit would overwrite,
and the timestamps are runtime-owned.
  value string    The new value, stored verbatim. The literal string "null" is TEXT, not a clear.
Omit it and pass `--clear` to remove a clearable attribute instead. (optional)

FLAGS
  --pretty          Render human-readable prose instead of the default JSON envelope. Opt-in: JSON is the zero-flag default so an agent never needs a flag to get parseable output. Never changes the exit code.
  --dense           Minify the envelope and elide the heavy `evidence` payload — token economy for an agent, in the SAME typed shape (no key is ever abbreviated). Never changes the exit code.
  --evidence        Keep the `evidence` payload under --dense. The escape hatch for a real investigation into a finding`s proof.

  --ref string      The requirement to update, as its stable key (e.g. TX-B6, G1) OR its UUID.
Tried as a UUID first, then as a key, so both spellings work everywhere a ref is accepted.
A ref that resolves to nothing is ERR_NOT_FOUND with did-you-mean suggestions.
Omit it and pass `--where` instead to update EVERY matching requirement.
  --clear           Remove the attribute rather than setting it. Mutually exclusive with `--value`.
A separate flag because argv cannot express JSON null, so "clear" and the literal string
"null" would otherwise be indistinguishable. (An `apply` op stream needs no such flag —
it writes `"value": null` directly.)
Refused on a non-clearable attribute, and refused on a slot the requirement`s OWN pattern
needs — clearing an event-driven requirement`s trigger would render "When , the ...".
  --where string    Bulk filter, as `<attr>=<value>`: apply the change to every requirement whose `<attr>`
equals `<value>`. Mutually exclusive with `--ref`.

a.message: ``l and a`symspec ym have semantically similar responses (cosine 1 ≥ 0.72) under the same system, but atomized to different atoms. No glossary merge is proposed: every merge of these phrasings either aliases a phrase to its own opposite under the committed antonyms (which turns the conflict into a redundancy) or re-points a phrase the committed vocabulary already unifies with another (which splits that atom). If they mean the same thing, rewrite one to use the same words as the other. These fire under the SAME trigger, so if they are polar OPPOSITES rather than synonyms, run `symspec antonym quasar nebula` instead — the formal tier will then treat them as contraries (they cannot both hold) and can prove the conflict. DESCRIPTION
  Set or clear one attribute on one requirement, or on every requirement matching a filter

USAGE
  symspec update [flags] <attr> [<value>]

ARGUMENTS
  attr string     The attribute to change. Legal values: patternType, preCondition, trigger, systemName, systemResponse, priority, status, verificationMethod, verificationNote, responseKind, stateEffect, stateConstraint.
NOT updatable, each for its own reason: `id` and `key` are immutable handles (every edge
references them), `sentence` is a denormalized rendering the next slot edit would overwrite,
and the timestamps are runtime-owned.
  value string    The new value, stored verbatim. The literal string "null" is TEXT, not a clear.
Omit it and pass `--clear` to remove a clearable attribute instead. (optional)

FLAGS
  --pretty          Render human-readable prose instead of the default JSON envelope. Opt-in: JSON is the zero-flag default so an agent never needs a flag to get parseable output. Never changes the exit code.
  --dense           Minify the envelope and elide the heavy `evidence` payload — token economy for an agent, in the SAME typed shape (no key is ever abbreviated). Never changes the exit code.
  --evidence        Keep the `evidence` payload under --dense. The escape hatch for a real investigation into a finding`s proof.
  --field string    Project the envelope down to comma-separated dotted paths (e.g. `data.verified,data.findings.0.code`), so a fix loop can read one value without a JSON tool. The result nests to mirror the requested paths; an unresolved path is omitted. Never changes the exit code.
  --ref string      The requirement to update, as its stable key (e.g. TX-B6, G1) OR its UUID.
Tried as a UUID first, then as a key, so both spellings work everywhere a ref is accepted.
A ref that resolves to nothing is ERR_NOT_FOUND with did-you-mean suggestions.
Omit it and pass `--where` instead to update EVERY matching requirement.
  --clear           Remove the attribute rather than setting it. Mutually exclusive with `--value`.
A separate flag because argv cannot express JSON null, so "clear" and the literal string
"null" would otherwise be indistinguishable. (An `apply` op stream needs no such flag —
it writes `"value": null` directly.)
Refused on a non-clearable attribute, and refused on a slot the requirement`s OWN pattern
needs — clearing an event-driven requirement`s trigger would render "When , the ...".
  --where string    Bulk filter, as `<attr>=<value>`: apply the change to every requirement whose `<attr>`
equals `<value>`. Mutually exclusive with `--ref`.

Zero matches is a successful no-op, so it is safe to run unconditionally.

a.message: ``l and a`symspec ym have semantically similar responses (cosine 1 ≥ 0.72) under the same system, but atomized to different atoms. No glossary merge is proposed: every merge of these phrasings either aliases a phrase to its own opposite under the committed antonyms (which turns the conflict into a redundancy) or re-points a phrase the committed vocabulary already unifies with another (which splits that atom). If they mean the same thing, rewrite one to use the same words as the other. These fire under the SAME trigger, so if they are polar OPPOSITES rather than synonyms, run `symspec antonym quasar nebula` instead — the formal tier will then treat them as contraries (they cannot both hold) and can prove the conflict. This is a suggestion, not a verdict.

No glossary merge is proposed: every merge of these phrasings either aliases a phrase to its own opposite under the committed antonyms (which turns the conflict into a redundancy) or re-points a phrase the committed vocabulary already unifies with another (which splits that atom). These fire under the SAME trigger, so if they are polar OPPOSITES rather than synonyms, run `symspec antonym quasar nebula` instead — the formal tier will then treat them as contraries (they cannot both hold) and can prove the conflict. import json, pathlib, subprocess
ROOT=pathlib.Path(__file__).parent
REPO=ROOT/'attack-copy'
mutants=[]
def add(file,original,replacement,operator,behaviors,tests,occurrence=0,control=False):
    source=subprocess.check_output(['git','-C',str(REPO),'show','HEAD:'+file],text=True)
    positions=[]; at=0
    while (at:=source.find(original,at))!=-1: positions.append(at);at+=len(original)
    assert positions, (file,original)
    start=positions[occurrence];end=start+len(original)
    def loc(i):return {'line':source.count('\n',0,i)+1,'column':i-source.rfind('\n',0,i)}
    a,b=loc(start),loc(end)
    mutants.append(dict(id='C'+str(len(mutants)+1).zfill(2),file=file,original=original,replacement=replacement,operator=operator,behaviors=behaviors,tests=tests,offset=start,location={'start':a,'end':b},span=f'{file}:{a["line"]}:{a["column"]}-{b["line"]}:{b["column"]}',control=control))

def sha(s):return hashlib.sha256(s).hexdigest()
def cmd(args,name,timeout=900):
 p=LOG/(name+'.log');t=time.time()
 with p.open('w') as out:
  child=subprocess.Popen(args,cwd=REPO,env=os.environ,stdout=out,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,start_new_session=True)
  try:code=child.wait(timeout=timeout)
  except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:os.killpg(child.pid,signal.SIGKILL);child.wait();code=124
 return dict(command=args,cwd=str(REPO),exitCode=code,seconds=round(time.time()-t,3),log=str(p),logSha256=sha(p.read_bytes()))
def test(tests,name,pattern=None):
 report=LOG/(name+'.json')
 r=cmd(['node_modules/.bin/vitest','run','--maxWorkers=2','--reporter=json','--outputFile='+str(report)]+(['-t',pattern] if pattern else [])+tests,name)
 if not report.exists(): r.update(status='timeout' if r['exitCode']==124 else 'oracle_error');return r
 j=json.loads(report.read_text()); fail=[a for t in j['testResults'] for a in t['assertionResults'] if a['status']=='failed']
 kills=[a['fullName'] for a in fail if not any('timed out' in s.lower() or 'timeout of' in s.lower() for s in a.get('failureMessages',[]))]
 r.update(report=str(report),reportSha256=sha(report.read_bytes()),passed=j['numPassedTests'],failed=j['numFailedTests'],total=j['numTotalTests'],files=len(j['testResults']),suites=j['numTotalTestSuites'],killedBy=kills,failureMessages=[{'name':a['fullName'],'messages':a.get('failureMessages',[])} for a in fail])
 r['status']='killed' if kills else 'survived' if r['exitCode']==0 and j['success'] and j['numTotalTests']>0 else 'timeout' if fail else 'oracle_error'
 return r

 specs=json.loads((ROOT/'mutants.json').read_text());out=[]
 if (ROOT/'results.json').exists():out=json.loads((ROOT/'results.json').read_text())
 for m in specs:
